summary.intent: Work through the post-0.10.2 Callisto plan (release rerun fix, test debt, docs refresh, init/derive refactors, SYS-NAPI), then speed up status/version/release at monorepo scale, adopt michi 0.6, and implement the tag-annotation hints proposed in ADR 13.
summary.outcome: Opened many PRs: #202-#208 (SYS-RETRY, mixed-routing test, docs refresh, init/derive refactors, SYS-NAPI), the performance stack #327/#328/#330/#333 (merged), michi 0.6 bump #336, confirmation-wave fix #337, ADR 13 #335, and hint writing #338; hint reading (part 2) and the full michi-pipeline move remain undone.

repo: Plan/tracking files like NEXT-WORK.md are local-only: keep them in .claude/plans/ and excluded via .git/info/exclude, never in a commit or PR (PR #201 was closed over this).
Always run `just ci` and read the log's own `exit=` line; the background task notification only reports the wrapper script's exit.

Release e2e harness (crates/callisto-cli/tests/common/release_harness.rs) allow-lists git calls and logs args with "$*", so multi-line tag messages looked like several commands; the allow-list needed cat-file --batch/--batch-check and the trace needed newline folding.
Tests that treated 'tag on HEAD' as released encoded the SYS-RETRY defect; they now tag an older commit.
Snapshots (insta) are committed on the old code first, then code is moved, so the refactors (R3 derive.rs split, R5b templates) are provably behavior-preserving.
The tag annotation lives only in the graph crate's prepared tag operation, not in the sealed intent, so ADR 13's claim that digests change was wrong and was corrected.
michi-graph 0.6 builds with no code changes; michi-pipeline steps must be 'static, which conflicts with the executor's borrowed non-cloneable intent proof.
The tag-ownership manifest read is a safety check against tags adopted by renamed or removed packages, so it should not be skipped just because a name is currently unique.
IdentityIndex::native_names/native_name/platforms_of were quadratic per package; fixed with a mutex-backed reverse-index cache, since the resolver trait requires Sync.
The status change meaning moved to net tree-id comparison, so a reverted edit no longer counts as changed.
macOS bash lacks mapfile and BSD sed rejects some one-liners, so the generated workflow template uses portable loops.

code.finding: TagHints writer and parser live together; the parser returns nothing unless version is exactly 1, there is one package, and tree lines are valid and unique, which gives the permanent fallback.
The derive function was split into stage functions with uploads_by_package moved into OpIndex, with characterization snapshots covering platform publish and error paths.
The napi roster is now derived per intent package by calling `callisto matrix`, and placement reads the plan job's napi_dirs output.

workflow: Write the failing reproduction first, and mutate the code to confirm new tests can fail; the plan's feedback rule is to prove with the real tool, not fakes.
Read the local checkout (~/Projects/michi) before fetching from crates.io; it was 83 commits behind origin/main, so read origin/main without touching the working tree.
An independent review agent on a risky PR (#202) surfaced real issues such as signed or multi-paragraph tag rejection.
The sandbox rejects inline env commands, heredocs and scripts mentioning git, so scripts are written to files first; edits are only allowed in the current worktree.
Benchmark carefully: a reported 2 GB cache speedup was a warm second pass, so use cold single-pass runs and hyperfine.
Quoted heredocs with escaped backticks leave literal backslashes in PR bodies; write bodies to files instead.
gh stack link and unstack manage native PR stacks, and a closed PR must be unstacked before relinking.

friction: Initially treated the plan as a PR (#201), which the user rejected and which required closing it.
Fetched michi from crates.io into a scratch crate instead of reading the local checkout; the user interrupted.
Sandbox restrictions repeatedly forced workarounds: no inline env, heredocs, or git-mentioning scripts, and edits only within the current worktree.
Background sessions could not edit the shared checkout, so the PR status could not be recorded in .claude/plans/NEXT-WORK.md.
Some CI runs failed from test-harness issues rather than product bugs (the init tests, three local.rs tests, the cat-file allow-list and trace newlines).
Earlier performance claims had to be corrected (the gix cache speedup and the 5x commit-id claim).
Cargo builds cannot run in parallel, so the planned parallel lanes were done serially.
The release PR #316 went stale after the performance stack merged.
open_items: Hint reading (ADR 13 part 2): the single for-each-ref returning trailers, skip logic, fallback tests for each case, an equivalence test, and spec criteria.
ADR 13 (#335) is still Proposed pending acceptance and the implementing PRs.
Regenerate and merge release PR #316 to ship 0.14.0.
Move the confirmation wave onto michi-pipeline (poll_step, precheck), which needs an ownership restructure or a scoped step API from michi; a single registry look can still overrun the window.
Adopt ready_by_edge when michi-graph PR #48 releases; the npm 0.6.0 package is held until 2026-10-24 02:55 UTC.
W0 branch cleanup is not done (about 35 local branches, plus the remote docs/next-work-plan, docs/spec-rewrite and fix/native-resolution) and needs the user's per-branch call.
W1 real-service credential check needs a decision on where it runs in CI.
Blocked on user decisions: D01 (SYS-MATURIN, W9), plus two W10 questions (graph edges for distinct target declarations, Python dev group cascade); W11 needs credentials and an approved run.
Remaining lanes: R1 walk.rs::build, W3 SYS-PYFILES/PYROUTES and W4, SYS-BARRIER, and W9.
#204 still lists SYS-RETRY/T08-RETRY and needs a follow-up once #202 merges; #202 had no review of its real gh/cargo/registry reads.
Remaining performance levers: a single tag listing instead of two, and the optional upstream gix issue on delta intermediates.
The RewriteKey and per-registry concurrency options from michi are not yet used.
